clue.text: Support collapsing rule in East Germany

indicators.note: something collapsing falls into a heap, so the letters of these words tumble into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east and D the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A regime's rule falls apart in the old East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Germany' tempts as DDR, but here it gives two separate abbreviations that go into the pool 'collapsing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie beneath something and hold it up is to support it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A type of candle half-heartedly burnt down further than before?

indicators.note: half of the doubled letter at the heart of the candle word is lost, leaving one of the pair

parts.note: tallow, rendered animal fat, is a traditional candle material and a candle type

explanation.surface: A candle of a certain kind burning down lower and lower, with little enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two central Ls of TALLOW, giving TALOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burnt down further than ever before has reached its lowest point, an idiomatic description, with the question mark flagging the candle-themed whimsy.

clue.text: She's possessive with love for leading man

parts.note: the possessive form of she is her
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman claims a leading man for her love.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male part in a play or film is the protagonist, the leading man.

clue.text: Regular letters from court posted carelessly around — found on this?

indicators.note: the jumbled word is wrapped around the picked letters
letters thrown down carelessly land jumbled, so the word posted is rearranged
taking letters at regular intervals from court, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Mail from a court, posted without care, turns up lying on the step outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' is the anagram signal and 'around' the insertion; 'Regular letters' takes the even letters of 'court'.
explanation.definitionFit: Post that is delivered is typically found lying on the step outside the front door, a cryptic pointer to the place.

clue.text: Loosen damaged nut securing handle incompletely

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the shortened handle within them
a damaged item is knocked out of shape, so the word nut is rearranged
the handle word is left unfinished, losing its last letter

parts.note: a knob is a round handle on a door or drawer

explanation.surface: A mechanic loosens a damaged nut that holds a broken handle in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals the anagram, 'incompletely' docks the handle's last letter, and 'securing' places the docked handle inside the rearranged nut.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a tangle or knot is to loosen it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Surrender as top player declared

indicators.note: something declared is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis tournament draw

explanation.surface: A leading player is declared to have given up the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or a point to another is to yield or surrender it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Partied without restraint on 20th, out to do this?

definitions.text: Partied without restraint on 20th, out to do this?

indicators.note: out signals the combined letters are put out of order
without means lacking, so the restraint word is removed from Partied

parts.note: a tie is something that binds or restrains
the number written out in full as a word

explanation.surface: Someone who partied wildly on the twentieth of the month went out to celebrate in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes TIE from PARTIED, leaving PARD; 'out' rearranges PARD, ON and TWENTIETH. Here '20th' is a number, not a pointer to 20-across. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celebrating wildly on a night out is going out on a spree, an idiom for exuberant partying.

clue.text: Computer program eastern ruler backed that should bear fruit

parts.note: an applet is a small computer program

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the two pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A piece of software and an Eastern monarch somehow promising a rich harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses E and ER to give REE.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard plant grown for its crop is expected to produce fruit, a playful description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Mimic voice holding power to attract

indicators.note: the first word holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: to ape is to mimic
P is the physics abbreviation for power
alto is a singing voice

explanation.surface: An impressionist's voice has the power to draw people in.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal to someone is to interest or draw them, a phrasal synonym for attract.

clue.text: Summoned royal forester

parts.note: rang means phoned or called someone up, summoning them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A forester was called to court by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper who patrols a forest or park is a warden of the woodland, a synonym.

clue.text: A while back you m-made a beastly noise and turned pale

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you
lowed means mooed like cattle, and the stammer of the clue doubles its first letter

explanation.surface: A stammering person whose voice turned into an animal noise went white.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'm-made' tells you to stammer the answer too: LOWED gains an extra L.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper or skin that has aged and lost colour has gone a sickly yellow hue, a past-tense verb synonym.

clue.text: Overcome, doctor gets personal

parts.note: own means personal, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: A physician, overwhelmed, takes things personally.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp or overwhelm someone, as a noise or a flood does, is to overcome them.

clue.text: Destroys what's built to last

indicators.note: something built is put together from parts, so the letters of to last are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A paradox: things made to endure end up wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal usage to write off a car completely in a crash is to wreck it, so destroys is a slang synonym.

clue.text: Meat's coming up — what happens if u snooze, sugar?

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: veal is calf meat
the saying goes you snooze, you lose, written here in text-speak

explanation.surface: Dinner is served: whoever dozes off misses out, sweetie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses VEAL to LAEV. 'u' is text-speak for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Fructose, the fruit sweetener, is also called by this older chemical name, so it is an example of a sugar.

clue.text: Al who sings, Ronnie who plays guitar and Dick who drums

parts.note: Al Green is an American soul singer
Ronnie Wood is a guitarist with the Rolling Stones
pecker is slang for dick, the penis

explanation.surface: A band line-up: a singer called Al, a guitarist called Ronnie and a drummer called Dick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick who drums' does double duty: 'Dick' supplies PECKER, and the whole phrase defines a bird that drums on trees. Dick is an old British slang word for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird hammers on tree trunks with its bill, so it drums; dicky-bird is British slang for any small bird.

clue.text: Tennis player opening in Wimbledon with ace — and again, controlling slippery surface

indicators.note: the doubled letters hold the ice surface within them, as if in control of it
and again means the same two letters come round a second time
the opening of Wimbledon is its first letter

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
an ice rink is a slippery surface for skating

explanation.surface: A tennis player opens at Wimbledon with an ace, then another, keeping control on a slippery court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and again' doubles WA to WAWA; 'controlling' puts RINK inside it. Stan Wawrinka is a Swiss Grand Slam champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Wawrinka is a Swiss professional who has won three Grand Slam titles, an example of a tennis player.

clue.text: Sailor favoured barrel in company of youth

definitions.text: Sailor favoured barrel in company of youth

indicators.note: the sailor's pieces go inside the company and youth letters

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
in means favoured or popular, as in being in with someone
Y stands for youth or young, as in the Y of a youth hostel association

explanation.surface: A popular sailor stowed in a barrel among young shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the sailor's pieces between the company letters and the youth letter. The whole clue also describes the answer: a young sailor in a ship's company.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster who serves officers and passengers aboard ship is a junior seaman, so a youthful sailor.

clue.text: Peer collapsed with pained sound

parts.note: fell means collapsed or toppled
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A lord fell over with a yelp of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, to look, or a lord; here it means an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is an equal or contemporary, as is a comrade or companion of the same standing.

clue.text: Endlessly sick following fast food from vegan place?

indicators.note: the shortened sick word comes after the fast

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: the word for sick loses its final letter

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Feeling off after a fast, someone turns to vegan cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse that is a staple of meat-free cooking, playfully said to come from a vegetarian kitchen, an example of plant food.

clue.text: Tone going round Brussels and Luxembourg in transit, perhaps,

indicators.note: going round means turning back the other way, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, so it stands for the European Union
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
a Ford Transit is a van, so travelling in one is going by van

explanation.surface: A dark shade on the move between two Benelux capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses EU+L+BY VAN. The Transit is the Ford van ubiquitous in Britain, printed without its capital to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark blue colour is a shade, and tone means a shade or tint of a colour.

clue.text: Dropping behind in referendum, say, one's undertaken to fulfil promise

indicators.note: dropping the behind means losing the tail end, the final letter

parts.note: a referendum is an example of a vote
one's read as one has, I've

explanation.surface: Falling behind in a referendum, a campaigner makes a pledge to keep a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping behind' cuts VOTE to VOT; 'one's' is I'VE, from 'one has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A votive offering is made in fulfilment of a vow, so it is something carried out to honour a promise.

clue.text: Indian side perhaps lagging after English got out, on one

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the shortened word is put beside the one letter
got out means removed, so the English letter is taken from the lagging word

parts.note: lagging means trailing behind
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the Indian team trailing after England's batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got out' removes E from BEHIND, leaving BHIND. 'Indian side' suggests a cricket team; it is a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra cooked Indian-style is served as an accompanying vegetable dish, an example of a side dish.

clue.text: Ditch Norwegian band after number two in chart

indicators.note: the band name comes after the single letter
number two in chart is its second letter

parts.note: a-ha is the Norwegian pop band behind Take On Me

explanation.surface: A Norwegian band dumped after reaching number two in the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken ditch with a wall bordering a park, keeping livestock out without blocking the view, is a landscape-garden feature.

clue.text: Mounted Republicans surrounding 10's partner

indicators.note: the party letters surround the partner's name

parts.note: GOP, Grand Old Party, is the nickname of the US Republican Party
Tonto is the partner of the masked lawman of the Western serials named at 10-across

explanation.surface: Mounted Republicans gather round the partner of a Western hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps the party's nickname round the sidekick. '10' refers to 10-across, the Lone ____ of radio and film Westerns.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb up onto a horse or a height is to mount it, so a phrasal synonym for mounted.

clue.text: Perhaps discharge firearm in front of king

indicators.note: the firearm comes first, ahead of the king letter

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Fire a gun in front of the king, perhaps as a salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' looks like a verb, to fire the firearm; it is a noun, sticky matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimy or sticky matter, such as that seeping from a wound or engine, is an example of an unpleasant mess.

clue.text: Madly in love with Romeo, knight is one unwilling to make the first move?

definitions.text: one unwilling to make the first move?

indicators.note: madly means wildly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A knight madly in love with Romeo hesitates to make the first move.
explanation.definitionFit: A painfully shy person hangs back and never takes the initiative, especially in romance.
